results.name: Cassoulet de Toulouse
results.short_description: Hearty casserole of white beans (lingots from the Lauragais plain), Toulouse sausage, duck or goose confit, pork belly, and pork rind, slow-cooked in an earthenware cassole.
results.strength_of_local_association: ★★★★★ — The city's most iconic dish; Toulouse is one of the three "cassoulet capitals" and claims its own distinct recipe.

results.name: Saucisse de Toulouse
results.short_description: Thick, coiled pork sausage lightly seasoned with garlic, pepper, and nutmeg, sold in a characteristic snail-shaped coil. Grilled, pan-fried, or used in cassoulet.
results.strength_of_local_association: ★★★★★ — Bears the city's name; ubiquitous at every Toulouse market stall.

results.name: Violettes de Toulouse
results.short_description: Crystallised violet petals coated in sugar, used in bonbons, liqueurs, syrups, and pastries. Toulouse has cultivated violets since the 19th century.
results.strength_of_local_association: ★★★★★ — Trademarked Toulouse specialty; the violet is one of the city's official symbols.

results.name: Fénétra
results.short_description: Medieval-origin layered tart with shortcrust pastry, almond cream, apricot or quince jam, and candied lemon. Traditionally baked for the Fête de la Fénétra.
results.strength_of_local_association: ★★★★★ — Unique to Toulouse; linked to the city's own annual festival.

results.name: Confit de canard
results.short_description: Duck legs slow-cooked and preserved in their own fat. A cornerstone of south-west French cuisine, prominently featured in Toulouse's cassoulet and market stalls.
results.strength_of_local_association: ★★★★ — Staple of Toulouse gastronomy, though shared with the wider south-west.

results.name: Magret de canard
results.short_description: Breast of a Moulard duck (raised for foie gras), seared like a steak and served pink. Often smoked as well.
results.strength_of_local_association: ★★★★ — A signature dish on virtually every Toulouse restaurant menu.

results.name: Foie gras de canard
results.short_description: Fattened duck liver, served mi-cuit (semi-cooked) or in terrines. Toulouse's Marché Victor Hugo is one of France's premier foie gras markets.
results.strength_of_local_association: ★★★★ — Central to Toulouse's culinary identity, though produced across the wider south-west.

results.name: Croustade aux pommes
results.short_description: Paper-thin, hand-stretched pastry layered with sliced apples, butter, and Armagnac. Also called *pastis gascon* or *tourtière* in neighbouring areas.
results.strength_of_local_association: ★★★★ — Widely sold in Toulouse bakeries and markets; closely tied to the city and its immediate hinterland.

results.name: Cachou Lajaunie
results.short_description: Small liquorice-flavoured pastilles created in 1880 by Toulouse pharmacist Léon Lajaunie, sold in a distinctive yellow tin.
results.strength_of_local_association: ★★★★★ — Invented and historically produced in Toulouse; an iconic local sweet.

results.name: Pavé du Capitole
results.short_description: Small chocolate praline shaped like the cobblestones of the Place du Capitole, Toulouse's main square.
results.strength_of_local_association: ★★★★★ — Created as a tribute to Toulouse's most famous square; sold exclusively as a Toulouse souvenir.
